courses.subject: SGCL
courses.title: Suicide Prevention and Crisis Intervention
courses.description: This course examines suicide as a school crisis in particular and as a specific crisis in the wider perspective of crisis intervention theory and applications. Students will be introduced to misconceptions of suicide, assessment of risk, critical incident stress debriefing, basic intervention skills, prevention, intervention, and postvention strategies.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA School Guidance & Counselling
courses.course_syllabus:
Suicidal behavior: Theories and classification; understanding self-injurious behaviour/ ethical issues; suicide assessment & prevention; crisis intervention/suicidal crisis; intervention

courses.subject: SGCL
courses.title: Career Exploration and Assessment Tools
courses.description: This course is designed to familiarize students with a variety of career exploration and assessment tools, including tools related to career interest, values, skills, and career decision making. Strategies and techniques in using career exploration and assessment tools to facilitate self-understanding and development in the context of career counseling and guidance are examined. Measurement principles and ethical guidelines relevant to career assessment are also introduced and discussed.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA School Guidance & Counselling
courses.learning_outcomes:
At the conclusion of the course, participants will be able to:
• Develop an understanding of Major Theories of Career Development
• Acquire some skills of using and interpreting career-related assessment tools
• Acquire some skills of Career Construction counselling (Life-Design)
• Understand the needs/concerns of The Career Development of youth with Specific Educational Needs

courses.subject: SGCL
courses.title: Cross-Cultural Counselling
courses.description: This course is designed to enhance the ability of counsellors to work with individuals from diverse cultural backgrounds based on a model of cross-cultural competence emphasizing awareness, knowledge and skills. Students are invited to examine their attitudes and beliefs toward different cultural groups, and to become aware of biases that might inhibit cross-cultural interactions. Selected theories and research on cross-cultural and multicultural counselling are introduced, with special attention paid to sub-cultures among the three Chinese societies. Students are also given the opportunity to learn and practice cross-cultural counselling skills and intervention strategies.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA School Guidance & Counselling
courses.course_syllabus:
Multicultural Counselling Competencies; Ethnic Identity & Racial Salience; Acculturation, Acculturative Stress, & Intergenerational Conflicts; Worldview & Value Orientations; Counselling Theories for Chinese

courses.subject: SGCL
courses.title: Interventions for Children with ADHD and Other Behavior Problems
courses.description: This course aims to help participants develop a comprehensive understanding of behavior problems among children in school settings, including attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and other externalizing behaviors such as impulsive, aggressive, and delinquent acts. The literature on managing children's behavior problems, including behavior modification programs, will be examined. School practitioners are encouraged to translate the basic knowledge they acquired through this course into relevant counseling and supporting strategies for working with children's behavior problems.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA School Guidance & Counselling
courses.learning_outcomes:
At the end of the course, participants will be able to:
1. develop an understanding of AD/HD and other externalizing behavioral problems in childhood.
2. acquire some intervention strategies and counseling techniques in helping children with externalizing behavioral problems and their families.
3. analyze critically of case treatment at individual and system levels related to children with externalizing behavioral problems.

(Individual course teachers may update the learning outcome as and whenever necessary.)
courses.course_syllabus:
Understanding AD/HD and other behavior problems; Developmental milestones for children’s externalizing behaviors; Role of executive functions in AD/HD and other related behaviors; Intervention approaches and medication issue

courses.subject: SGCL
courses.title: Understanding Specific Learning Difficulties
courses.description: This course aims to provide participants with a sound understanding of the core issues of specific learning difficulties/disabilities (SLD). Drawing on recent research developments in the field of SLD, attempts will be made to demystify this subject, as well as to examine the latest research findings on the mechanisms underlying various types of SLD. Characteristics of and differentiations among different types of SLD (e.g., dyslexia, specific language impairment, developmental coordination disorder) will be reviewed and discussed. The central premise of this course is that teachers and helping professionals, equipped with sound knowledge, will be able to establish their own working principles in helping students with SLD.
